scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8878: Users in both pods report the "web2.local" portal
returns nothing -- connections fail immediately instead of loading. The other
portals (web0/web1/web3) load fine. DNS resolves web2.local to 10.200.0.5,
and ping to 10.200.0.5 works from user machines. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_2

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_2 Apache (apache2) HTTP service
Mechanism: the apache2 service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) is stopped, so
  nothing listens on TCP/80 and connection attempts are refused immediately.
  Everything below the service layer is healthy: DNS still resolves
  web2.local -> 10.200.0.5, the OSPF path delivers packets (ping succeeds),
  and the other three web servers keep serving. The symptom is purely the
  dead HTTP daemon on one server.
Localization: web_server_2
Root cause: apache2 not running on web_server_2 (TCP/80 closed)
Fix: `service apache2 start` on web_server_2
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_2 (e.g. `service apache2 start`
/ `systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache listens on port 80 again,
http://web2.local serves normally. Nothing else needs changing.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The Apache2 web server daemon on `web_server_2` (10.200.0.5) — the service process responsible for handling HTTP requests on port 80.

**Mechanism:** When a client connects to port 80 on `web_server_2`, the Linux kernel finds no socket bound to that port and immediately responds with a TCP RST. This causes curl (and any browser) to receive an instant connection failure (HTTP code 000) with near-zero elapsed time (≈0.003 s), which matches the helpdesk description of "returns nothing — connections fail immediately." ICMP (ping) continues to work because it is handled by the kernel network stack, not by the application daemon, so the host is reachable at L3 while the service is completely dark.

**Localization:** The fault is isolated to `web_server_2` only. All three peer servers (`web_server_0`, `web_server_1`, `web_server_3`) run apache2 with 3 worker processes and respond HTTP 200 from localhost. On `web_server_2`, `ps aux` shows only PID 1 (`bash`) — the apache2 binary is installed (`/usr/sbin/apache2`) and web content exists under `/var/www/html`, but no apache2 process has ever been started or has survived.

**Root cause:** The apache2 daemon is absent on `web_server_2` — either it was never launched at container start, or it was stopped/killed after startup — leaving port 80 unbound and causing every inbound HTTP connection to be immediately refused.

**Fix:** Start apache2 on `web_server_2`: run `apache2 -k start` (or `service apache2 start`) inside the container. To make it persistent across restarts, ensure the container startup script mirrors the configuration used by the other web server containers.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) as the affected device.
The report explicitly states apache2 on web_server_2 is not running and port 80 is unbound/closed, causing immediate TCP connection refusals.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path
per_axis.rationale: The report rules out IP-layer/network reachability (ping) but does not explicitly state that DNS resolves web2.local to 10.200.0.5, so it doesn't fully exonerate DNS.
The remediation explicitly instructs starting the apache2 service on web_server_2 (service/apache2 -k start), which matches the expected fix and will restore port 80 listening.

The log contains direct observations: ICMP reachability is OK, service/pressure sweeps flagged web_server_2, and an exec_shell on web_server_2 shows only PID 1 (bash), no apache2 processes, and no listener on :80 while a healthy peer does have apache2 and a bound :80—so the conclusion that apache2 is stopped is well supported. The inference that this causes immediate TCP connection refusals and the recommended 'service apache2 start' fix follow logically and the investigation ruled out lower-layer causes.
